operator.name: propose_sequence
operator.description: Propose what sends on its own, as a card the person approves (every such thing is a sequence): a message sent once, a sequence at a moment of the customer journey or on a list, a whole new sequence with its steps, a step added, changed, taken away or given new words, a draft started or let go, people taken out, a batch waiting for an OK approved or skipped, a sequence paused, resumed, renamed or retimed, its channels, a new saved message, and cold email to leads. Action once takes template_id, one message (the id of any of its versions, as sequences with action lists lists it), and proposes sending it to an audience, everyone whose yes covers it (a reminder or a confirmation the yes to messages, an offer or news the yes to offers) or any list sequences with action lists names (audience_kind everyone; list for a People list, with its id as audience_id; saved for one of the workspace's own, with its audience_id), with params as the message's values in order (typed text, or @first_name, @business_name, @booking_link or @review_link, the link its Google listing keeps for a review, to fill per person), an optional scheduled_for as an ISO time with its offset (2026-09-20T15:00:00-04:00, never a bare date), an optional name, and optional channels (whatsapp, sms, email; whatsapp when none is named, so for a message that holds email or text name the channels its `channels` in sequences with action lists say it holds): each person is reached once, on the first it can, and a channel the workspace cannot send on, or the message has no version for, is refused. Action moment takes trigger and proposes a standing rule that sends one message to newly eligible people who said yes: trigger is quiet_30 (win-back by silence, nothing heard in 30 days, where no calendar is connected), lapsed (win-back by appointments, none in 45 days, where a calendar is connected), visit_tomorrow (a reminder the day before an appointment) or visited (a check the day after one), both only where a calendar is connected and each sent whatever else the person hears from you within a week of it, everyone_monthly (the month's offer), saved_list (on any list: its token from sequences with action lists in list, one of People's or one of the workspace's own, with policy_class campaign for an offer or reengage for a win-back), or proposal_waiting (the proposal follow-up: one nudge per proposal waiting past the workspace's pace, one such playbook per workspace, its message carrying the proposal's link as @proposal_link), a moment this workspace is not offered being refused in words to say; template_id is a message from sequences with action lists (the id of any of its versions), or omitted for the trigger's starter, which the card adds at its Approve where the workspace does not hold it yet (its WhatsApp version then goes to WhatsApp for review where none is on file, which the card says), but for a starter that takes words of its own such as the month's offer; starter, in place of template_id, is the moment's starter to file at Approve where the workspace does not hold it yet, by its key: on visited, after_visit_review is the thank-you with a review ask, only where the Google listing keeps a review link, and after_visit_check, the thank-you that asks how it went, is the one taken when none is named; params are the message's values in order (typed text, or @first_name, @business_name, @booking_link, @review_link, the link its Google listing keeps for a review, @visit_when and @visit_service on an appointment's moment, or @proposal_link), filled in for a starter except a typed one such as the month's offer; run_hour is 9 to 20 by the business's clock (default 10), cap_per_run defaults to 25, and channels (whatsapp, sms, email; when none is named it goes by every one the workspace can send on now that the message holds, as a new playbook opens in Campaigns, and the card says which, so name them only to go by fewer, or by one that is not ready yet) are the ones it may go by, each person once on the first it can: a channel its purpose never carries is refused, and one the workspace cannot send on yet is kept, its runs holding those people until it can; until is its last day, YYYY-MM-DD by the business's clock, today or later, after which it runs nothing. A new one starts with the mode its class's Autonomy row says (decision 0064), and its first batch waits for an OK whatever that is, which the card says. Action make proposes a whole new sequence to customers: first, its first step exactly as action moment takes it (a moment or a list, its message by template_id, its clock and channels), then up to 3 steps after it (each a wait, what must still hold, its message), and start (true starts it once approved, false keeps it as a draft). Write each message first with action message where the Library has none, in a plan. Action step adds a step after the last (after_days and template_id), or changes one after the first by step_id: its wait, what must still hold, its channels, name or values. A step's message is changed with action words. Action step_remove takes away a step after the first, with the steps after it. Action words gives a step a different message from now (write it first with action message); where WhatsApp has to approve it, the step keeps sending its own until then. Action start turns a draft on: its first step runs from its next run. A paused one is resumed with action change. Action run_now runs a sequence's first step now, as its hourly run would: it waits for an OK where its class asks. Action change takes playbook_id, a playbook that exists, as sequences with action moments gives it (or the page's rows), and only what they asked to change: state (paused stops its next runs; running starts them again under its own mode), name (at most 80 characters), run_hour (9 to 20 by the business's clock), cap_per_run (1 to 500 people a run), gap_days (7 to 365 days before a person is reached again), cadence_days (1 to 90, the month's offer alone), params (its message's values in order, as action moment takes them: new text in the same message, never a new message), until (its last day, YYYY-MM-DD by the business's clock, today or later; it runs nothing after) or mode (how its batches are decided, its "Before each batch": ask, each waits for an OK; veto, each waits 30 minutes for a Stop, then goes; auto, each goes on its own, never for a sequence to leads; a batch of new words waits for an OK whatever it says). Nothing else about it moves: its moment, message and list are its drawer's, and its channels are action channels'. A run already waiting for approval stays waiting after a pause, and the card says so: propose action batch with verb skip beside it when they want that run gone. A sequence to leads (cold email) takes state and mode alone here, its emails and steps being its page's; anything else asked of one, a value outside its bounds and a playbook that already reads so are refused in words; a part of the change it already holds (a pause of one paused) is left off the card, which says so, and the answer says it too. Action channels takes playbook_id, a playbook that exists, as sequences with action moments gives it, and channels (whatsapp, sms, email), every channel it should go by from now on, not only the ones to add (that read gives the channels it goes by now): each person is reached once, on the first of them that can reach them, so one more channel widens who it reaches and never sends a person two messages. Nothing else about the playbook changes. A channel its purpose never carries is refused; one it cannot go by yet (no line, no version of its message there, offers by email not open) is kept, and the card says it waits and that its runs hold those people until it can; a run of it already waiting for approval keeps the channels it was made with, and the card says so; and a playbook that already goes by exactly those channels is refused in words. Action batch takes broadcast_id, a playbook's run that waits for a person, as sequences with action moments (a playbook's waiting) or action sent (waiting_on_you) gives it, and verb: approve, which sends it now (asked outside the hours a message may go out in, between 9:00 and 20:59 by the business's clock, it goes at 9:00), or skip, which ends this run unsent and leaves the playbook running. Always give verb, from their words: it has no default, and the card says it back. A run made for a day that has passed can only be skipped, and a batch to leads (cold email) is approved or skipped the same way, its card saying what the check held. Action leave takes people or leads out of a sequence; a send of theirs not yet gone is skipped with them. Action decide answers an email the check held: include lets it go as it is, rewrite writes its opening again, skip leaves it out of this batch, not_a_fit sets its business aside. Nothing undoes it. Action sent_by_hand records what became of an email handed over to send by hand from the business's own inbox: sent, or not_sent. Ask them; never say one went that they did not say. Action discard takes away a draft that never sent; one that has been on is paused instead. Action message writes a new message for the Library and proposes it as a card: name (snake_case), language (en or es, as the rule for a message's language says; another language is another card under the same name, called together), category marketing (an offer or the business's news) or utility (about their own appointment or proposal, which needs a whatsapp version), versions, each optional and at least one (whatsapp {body}, email {subject, body}, sms {body}, never sms for marketing), and slots naming the values {{1}}, {{2}} in order (position, label, kind: text, first_name, business_name, booking_link or review_link). Read sequences with action messages first: a name the Library holds in that language is refused. A whatsapp version needs a connected number and goes to WhatsApp's review; email needs email set up. Your versions are a first draft that the message writer rewrites before the card is shown: put the facts in them (the offer in their words and figures, its days), never a price they did not give. The card quotes every version; Approve files it, and nothing is sent. Action cold_email proposes a cold email sequence to the businesses of a search or a list of chosen leads (propose_leads with action list makes one): its emails, their waits and its pace, from the workspace's own mailboxes (or handed over to send by hand). Its first run is planned once approved and waits for their say before an email goes. Write like a person to one business; never claim a relationship that does not exist. Action leads adds leads to a reach-out fed by a list (one made from leads chosen or imported, not a search's own): root_id is the reach-out's id (reach_out on leads with action lead, or the reach-out the page has open), lead_ids the leads' ids from leads. The card says first what the add would do -- how many would join and why each other would not (already written to, a customer, no checked address, with another reach-out) -- by the add's own rule, and is refused in words when none would. It sends nothing and approves no run: the reach-out's next run plans the first email and waits for their say. A reach-out a search keeps current is refused: its search's new leads join it by themselves. For an offer, a promotion or a whole setup, call propose_plan with action offer instead. Read sequences first: action list and action sequence for what exists and its ids, action lists for who can be sent and the messages a send may use, action moments for the moments offered. When nobody can be sent a message, say why: nobody said yes (point to their profiles) or the ones who did have no number to send to, or no channel that can carry it now (the lists read says which); never propose a send to nobody. A starter the workspace does not hold yet is added at the card's Approve, a typed value left blank is refused in words, and a second running sequence on the same moment, list and message is refused unless they name it apart. A person reads campaign or sequence, never playbook or broadcast; the fields keep those names.

operator.name: propose_settings
operator.description: Propose a settings change as a card the person approves, by action: what the receptionist knows (closed days, hours, a note, a service), how it answers (its voice, languages, what callers hear and who they reach, your own words, the messages when it can't answer, photos), what it may do alone for a class of message (autonomy), or the business's goal for you. Action autonomy changes what the receptionist may do alone for a whole class of message: class with mode, or the reply confidence dial (min_confidence) alone. Call it when they want the receptionist to act on its own, wait for them, or hold its replies for a look; propose_person with action mode is for one person. Each class takes the modes its row on the Autonomy page offers (veto holds a reply, or the reply to a review, so a person can stop it), and a mode a class does not take is refused in that page's words. For reengage, campaign and follow_up the row is what a NEW sequence starts as (decision 0064): each existing sequence keeps its own mode, changed by propose_sequence's change with its mode; a sequence that should not send is paused, so those rows take no never. Never for money: that class is locked by charter, so a request to change it is answered in words, not proposed. The modes as they stand are in this prompt above, so no read is needed first. Action answer_style keeps how this person likes your answers (length, format, language) as their own note, which comes with each of their questions from then on; empty clears it, and it replaces the one they keep. Call it when they want answers a way beyond this conversation ("always bullets", "every time in Spanish", "next time, shorter"); a shape asked for within one conversation is kept there without it. Theirs alone, never a teammate's, and they see and change it in Settings › Profile.

operator.name: propose_thread_verb
operator.description: Propose an Inbox action on a thread: take_over (a person answers from here), hand_back (the receptionist resumes), snooze (until an ISO time with its offset, or by default tomorrow at 10:00 by the business's clock), wake, archive, or resolve (close the open escalation; the thread stays). conversation_id is the id a read returned. Call it when they ask to take, hand back, snooze, wake, archive or resolve a thread; a reply is propose_reply with action draft, and how the receptionist treats one person is an owner's to set (propose_person with action mode). It refuses in words when the action does not fit the thread's state: nothing to resolve, not snoozed, or nobody to hand back from.

operator.name: report
operator.description: The Reports page for any window its period control picks -- a period (7d, 30d, 90d or month: month is the days since the 1st), days picked (from and to, YYYY-MM-DD, at most ninety, ending today at the latest), or a shortcut (yesterday, last_week, last_month), 30d where none is named -- and only the lenses asked for (lenses: overview, campaigns, reviews, cold_email, receptionist, people; every one where none is named). The overview: messages answered by the receptionist, by a person and left unanswered, the median and p90 reply time (both include the hold the owner set before a reply goes out; reply_time.hold splits the replies against it: with no hold, as the hold ended, or later, and the most any took past it), calls and their minutes, new people, the escalation reasons, the change against the period before, a by-day series, the booking line (asked, then booked) where the calendar is read, the Deals section where a deal was ever recorded, and the Campaigns lens, as the page says it: head is its sentence; figures are the people sent to, the share of the messages delivered, the share of those people who wrote back, and the yeses and stops after a campaign, each against the period before; funnel is what was sent, delivered, read (WhatsApp's alone) and answered, counted in messages (a person sent three is three messages here and one in figures); by_channel is the same by channel where more than one sent (read is a share of what went by WhatsApp alone: a text or an email keeps no read receipt); sources are the five that sent the most; window is the period's, from the database's ledger: held (who was held back, and why), runs_stopped (the runs that failed or were canceled), failed_sends (why sends failed after they left), by_message (who wrote back to each message), send_to_first_reply (how soon the first reply came) and wait_for_your_ok (how long approvals waited); stuck is what is stuck now, whatever period is picked: the runs waiting for your OK, the failed runs, the replies waiting on you, the messages Meta stopped and your WhatsApp number; a share is said only of five or more and a count under that, and a mix with nothing to draw says the page's words in empty; window is null where the database does not keep the ledger yet and stuck where it does not keep what is stuck, each with an error beside it where its read failed, and a part of window the database did not count is null too; campaigns says error where its numbers could not be read. The Reviews lens is in reviews: the sentence at its head and its figures as the page says them (the rating, the count, the reviews written against the period before) and, where the owner's Business Profile is connected, how many were answered and how fast, the mix of stars, and how many wait for a reply (held is how many of the oldest waiting hold a reply the receptionist wrote and did not post), the oldest five waiting in rows and the newest five in latest, each with its id; reviews says linked false where no Google listing is linked, and error where its numbers could not be read. The Reach-outs section is in reach_outs, as the page says it: strip is the emails the reach-outs wrote, the share that landed and the number that bounced, each against the period before; emails is what was written, delivered and bounced, counted in emails; businesses is the businesses written to and how many wrote back, were interested, booked or said no, counted in businesses as they stand now (each counts once, at the last email that wrote to it, and an outcome is set against nothing before); angles is who wrote back, as they stand now, by the opening of the last email; handed is the line on the businesses handed to the owner, null where none were, and empty says nothing was written; reach_outs is null where the workspace has no reach-out, and error where its numbers could not be read. The Receptionist lens is in receptionist, as the page says it: what became of the replies held before they went out (hold), what customers asked about (topics), the languages the receptionist wrote in where it wrote in more than one, how the calls someone spoke on ended, the booking link and how many of the people it went to have booked since (link), your first reply after a handover and the time to settle one (handover), the missed calls answered within an hour (missed), what came while the business was closed and how many of those the receptionist answered (closed), and what is stuck now (stuck: who waits on you, call-backs, the replies held back), with held_back giving the reasons the send door refused a reply; receptionist says available false where the database does not keep these numbers yet, and error where they could not be read. The People lens is in people, as the page says it: head is its sentence; window is the period, counted in people (one who wrote ten times is one): reached (who reached you, how many were new, the yeses won and the stops, each against the period before), channels (how they reached you), first_came (how the new ones first came), yeses and stops (who gave them), steps_done (the steps finished and how many on their day) and email_stopped (the addresses that stopped working); book is everyone as they stand now, whatever period is picked: wires (the ways they reach you), fresh (how long since they last wrote or called, with quiet saying how many have been quiet over 30 days), stuck (the steps overdue and due today, and the email that stopped working) and stand (how many said yes to messages, can receive offers, opted out or are quiet); a mix with nothing to draw says the page's words in empty; people says window null where the database does not keep the period's numbers yet, book null where the people could not be counted, available false where neither could be read, and error where they could not be read. Call it for how a period went or for a trend, naming only the lenses the question needs; the today tool has the day itself and its counts, and the Reports page on screen already holds this. An empty period says so in empty; a window the report cannot answer is an error, said in the page's words.

operator.name: sequences
operator.description: Everything that sends on its own, as Campaigns reads it (every such thing is a sequence), by action: the sequences, one sequence's steps and people, the moments of the customer journey a sequence can start at, who a send can go to and the messages it may use, the Library, what went out and how it did, the journey, and cold email to leads. Action list reads every sequence as the Sequences page lists them: each with its sequence_id, name, group, what starts it, state, line, steps and who is in it, and what waits on the owner (needs_you); needs_you on top is the page's count. Action sequence reads one as its record shows it: when it starts and stops, the mode its batches go under (and batches_did: what its batches did over the last 90 days, how many went after an OK or on their own, stopped or skipped unanswered: the evidence a mode is set on), its one notice, its steps with their ids (wait, message, channels, last 30 days), who is in it by where they stand (in_it: the first 25, each with its contact_id or lead_id), what waits on the owner (waiting_on_you: each held or handed-over email by its send_id, for propose_sequence with action decide or sent_by_hand), and its last five batches. Action moments reads the sequences that start at a moment as the page shows them, standing rules that each send one message to newly eligible people who said yes: each with its playbook_id, what starts it, its message (template), its channels, its clock and next run (next_run, null where it runs nothing: runs_nothing says why, and ended the day one ended), its last day ahead (ends), its state in the page's words, its own mode (mode: how its batches are decided, mode_words says each, and next_batch_asks_first where its next batch waits for an OK because its words are new), its list when it runs on one, what it sent and how many replied over the last 30 days (null where that could not be read), and a batch waiting for a person; then every moment this workspace can use, with who it names now: said_yes_now (who said the yes its message needs, a number or not) and can_be_sent_now (who of them a run reaches), and each one's starter message. Action lists, read before any send, lists who a send may go to: everyone who said yes, every People list this workspace can count, and every list of the workspace's own, each with its kind and audience_id (what propose_sequence with action once takes), its list token (what people with action search takes), and four counts, because there are two consents and a yes needs a number to send to and a channel to carry it: can_be_sent_offers and can_be_sent_messages (who a promotional, or a utility or authentication, message reaches on WhatsApp) and said_yes_to_offers and said_yes_to_messages (everyone who gave that yes, as People counts it, whether or not a number or a channel can carry it now), with why_none_offers or why_none_messages where some said yes and WhatsApp reaches none of them, saying what they lack in People's words. It says which channels carry offers now (offers_go_by), and also lists, under templates, the messages a send may use, each with its template_id (any of its versions' ids names the message), category, channels (true for each of whatsapp, email and sms it can be sent on now; a message that holds email or sms is proposed with channels naming them, and its card then counts the people those channels reach, so a 0 in the four counts above does not mean nobody can be reached), values and body, why a WhatsApp version this product cannot send whole is left out (cannot_send), and whether the number may send and its daily limit, since a send reaches only a recorded yes with a number to send to. Action messages reads the Library whole: every message, a name in a language, with its category, each version on its channel with its state (approved, pending while WhatsApp reviews it, rejected, paused or disabled), the values it fills and the sequences that send it (used_by). Call it before a new message is written, so the Library never holds a twin; to pick a message a send can use now and say who it reaches, call action lists instead. Action sent reads what went out as the page lists it, the recent fifty, with older saying whether there are more: each batch with its name, whether a campaign or a person sent it, who it went to and its message, its state in the page's words (one waiting for a person to approve it has waiting_on_you; one whose day has passed is too_late_to_approve), when, how many it was for, how many were sent (sent_by_channel, where it went by more than one), the share of those delivered, the share of those sent by WhatsApp that were read (a text or an email keeps no read receipt), and how many replied, were held back and failed, with why one failed. Action batch reads one batch as its opened run shows it: its row, the five figures (sent, delivered, replied, said yes, asked to stop), the people it touched in the page's words, and what came back, quoted. It returns at most 20 people and 10 replies, the figures counting everyone. Action journey reads the customer journey: how many of its moments are covered (covered, of), then each stage in the order a customer passes it (first contact, the day before and the day after an appointment, which need a calendar, a proposal waiting where a deal was ever recorded or a sequence stands on it, quiet or lapsed) with whether it is covered, its state, the moment a sequence on it starts from and the sequences that stand on it; and guide, what each touch point sends and when. An offer or a whole setup is one call of propose_plan with action offer, which reads the journey itself and makes the steps, never a sequence proposed stage by stage from this read. Action cold_emails reads the cold email sequences to leads: each with its root_id, name, the search or list of leads it writes to, whether it runs, its emails, its pace, whether the owner sends each from their own inbox, and who is in it (waiting, writing, done). Read action lists before a send, and to say who a message would reach; action moments to say what is running, and before a new sequence at a moment. Pick the message first, then quote its can_be_sent count as who it reaches, never a larger one, for a message that goes by WhatsApp; for a message whose channels hold email or sms, propose it with channels naming them and quote the card's count, since the can_be_sent counts are by WhatsApp alone and a 0 there does not mean nobody can be reached; when a WhatsApp message's count is 0 and its said_yes is not, and its channels hold no other, the ones who said yes cannot be sent it: say how many said yes and what they lack, as the audience's why_none words say it (a number to send to, or a channel that can carry it, which offers_go_by names), and never send the owner to get a yes they already have. When a moment's can_be_sent_now is 0 and said_yes_now is not, the ones who said yes have no number to send to, no channel that can carry it now (action lists' offers_go_by names which), or hear from you within a week of today: say so the same way. A list that cannot be counted here carries cannot_count and no counts; a null count means the page could not count it just now, and nothing has run because it was read. A person reads campaign or sequence, never playbook or broadcast; the fields keep those names.

sequence_id.description: A sequence's id, from action list.

broadcast_id.description: A batch's id, from action sent or a moment's waiting batch.

operator.name: signals
operator.description: What stands out across the workspace now, computed from its pages, each with its numbers and the cards that fit it: a follow-up of yours that is due, people with nothing sending on its own, lists that feed nothing, leads nobody writes to, a search that asks a question, replies and batches waiting, people never asked for the yes to offers, deals with no next step; and the owner's goal. Read it at the start of a conversation, when they ask what to do next or how to get more customers, and before proposing a plan of your own. It takes nothing and changes nothing.

operator.name: today
operator.description: The Today page as it stands: who needs a person right now, the WhatsApp threads whose free-reply window is closing while the customer waits, today's calls, the standing of the receptionist, a recap and the day's counts. Start here for 'how are we doing', 'what needs me' or 'brief me', and read it for what Today holds when the person is on another page. needs_you counts the holds and the replies counting down to send in your name (replies_on_their_way, which it does not list: inbox with action list has them); campaign_runs_waiting are the runs waiting for your say: those an approval can still send, and going reach-out runs whose check holds emails for you (sequences with action sent lists them); going_today is what goes on its own later today unless it is stopped (a batch held for a stop, a message sent once and set for later, a reach-out's run), each with when it goes, as Today's Going today draws it; searches_waiting stopped to ask you. It holds no drafts: inbox with action list and filter held has them, and inbox with action thread has a whole conversation. Nor the bell's notifications, what was sent to this person: workspace with action notifications reads them. needs_you and calls are capped, the counts are not; nothing changes because it was read.

operator.name: workspace
operator.description: The workspace, by action. Action settings takes nothing more and reads the settings as the receptionist runs on them: the business and its time zone, hours, closures, services, languages, guardrails, notes, booking rules, when it escalates, whether the calendar and vision are on, the notifications (where alerts are emailed), the autonomy rows with their modes and limits (the reply policy's dials among them), and which channels are connected with their numbers. Call it for the reply policy's dials, the channels and the notifications; the hours, closures, services, notes, guardrails, booking notes and the autonomy modes are already in this prompt, so answer those from here without a read. A channels read that failed is said in could_not_read, never as no channels; propose_settings is what changes a setting. Action connections takes nothing more and reads what the workspace is connected to, in the Setup page's words: whether the receptionist answers and on which numbers; its phone line and whether the number its customers know is forwarded to it, WhatsApp, the email mailbox, the calendar and Google, each with its state and what the page says of it; and each mailbox it writes its reach-outs from, with its state, its day, its ramp and what to do next. Call it for whether something is connected, or why not; action settings has the receptionist's own rules. Billing and the plan's price are not here: money stays out of Ask. Action notifications takes nothing more and reads this person's own notifications as the bell keeps them on the server: the last thirty days, sixty at most, newest first, each with its title, its first line, how long ago, whether it is unread for them and where it opens, and how many are unread; one they dismissed is gone. Call it for what the bell has told them. The bell also shows what the page works out in the tab (threads waiting on a person, missed calls, invitations), which this cannot read, so say the bell may hold more; billing's notices stay out of Ask. Nothing changes because it was read.

partner.name: calendar
partner.description: The owner's calendar as the receptionist reads it. Action week takes day and an optional days and reads a day or a few: what is taken (in the calendar's own words, with the person in People when the title names one, and its visit_id), whether the business is closed that day, and the windows the receptionist would offer; day is today, tomorrow, a weekday (mon..sun), a date (YYYY-MM-DD), or empty for the page's own week, and days is how many from there, at most 14. Action openings takes day and service and reads the open times from the connected calendar, against the business hours, closures and booking rules, as the receptionist would offer them to a caller: a state, a sentence, and the open windows day by day, sized for a service when one is named; day is a weekday (mon..sun), a date (YYYY-MM-DD), or empty for the next days, and service is the service's name to size the slot, or empty. Action room takes nothing more and reads how full the book is over the next 14 days (days; fewer where the business offers times fewer days ahead), for pacing an offer to what the business can take: open, how many slots of the business's slot length are free against its hours, closures and booking rules once the calendar's appointments and the bookings on record are taken out, as the receptionist would offer them; by_day, the open slots of each day that has any (day is YYYY-MM-DD on the business's clock); and taken, how many slots of the same hours those appointments and bookings fill. A slot is the calendar's, one booking at a time, and never a count of staff or seats: say open as the room left in the book, never as how many people can come at once. none says no_calendar where no calendar feed is connected and unavailable where it could not be read, and the counts then say nothing of the book. Call action week for what a day looks like or who is booked when, action openings for when there is room or what is free on a day, the free slots alone, sized to a service, and action room for how full the book is over the next fourteen days, to pace an offer. Openings need a connected calendar feed, said in the workspace's facts above. Taken is the owner's own calendar and open is what the receptionist would offer; nothing is booked from here, since customers book through the booking link, or with the team where there is none.

partner.name: calls
partner.description: Phone calls, as the Calls page and a call's page read them. Action list takes filter and lists calls newest first: who, when, how long, how it ended, a one-line summary, and the ids of the call, its conversation and the person; filter is missed (today's missed calls), abandoned (today's inbound callers who reached the receptionist and hung up within seconds, so they got nothing), today, live (on the line now), or recent (newest first). Action get takes call_id, the id a row here, the today tool or people with action get returned, and reads one call: who, when, how long, how it ended, its summary, the state of its recording, the caller's contact id, and the transcript turn by turn. Call action list to find calls by day, outcome or whether they are live, and a live call before proposing a whisper; a count of calls is the today tool's or the page's own, since the rows here are capped. Call action get when the transcript or the full summary is needed and the page on screen holds only the call's row. list returns at most 20 calls from the newest hundred; nothing changes because it was read. get caps the transcript at 40 turns, with transcript_turns saying how many there are; a call the workspace does not hold is an error, said in words.

partner.name: guide
partner.description: How Chanlytics works, page by page, for this member: what each page is for, what you can do there for them by card (tool and action), what stays on the page and why, and what Setup says is missing and what each missing piece stops. Read it when they ask what you can do, where something is, or how to start; for a new owner, before anything else. With skill customer_message it answers that skill's guide instead: what to hand the writer that rewrites a message's words for customers. It changes nothing.

partner.name: inbox
partner.description: The Inbox, on every wire (WhatsApp, text or email, whichever the customer last wrote on, named in channel). Action list takes filter and finds threads: needs_you (what waits on you, as the Inbox counts it: a hold nobody has taken, or a reply counting down that can still be stopped), held (a draft waiting to send), waiting (taken over by a person), snoozed, or recent (all, newest first); each row has its state, its held draft when one waits, how long the customer has waited, whether the reply window is open, and its last three messages with who wrote them. Action thread takes conversation_id, the id a row here, the today tool or people returned, and an optional more, and reads one conversation: the person, its state, the open escalation, whether the reply window is open, the held draft with why it was held, and the messages with who wrote each and why the receptionist answered or held as it did. Action search takes words, what to look for, and an optional days, and finds them in what was said: every message of the workspace (what customers wrote; what the receptionist or the team wrote to them, sent or not; and a call's note in its thread) and every call's transcript, newest first, none older than days back from now (30 unless asked, at most 90). Call it for a word, the name of a thing or a phrase, such as did anyone mention parking this month; call action list for threads by their state, and action thread for one whole conversation, which a message hit's conversation_id opens (calls with action get opens a call hit's call_id). words are looked for as they were written or said, in English or Spanish, never stemmed, so park does not find parking: when nothing is found, try the other form; "a phrase in quotes" finds the words together, -word leaves out what holds it, or finds either side, and words that only leave things out find nothing. It returns at most 20 hits, with shown and more_available (whether there are more), each a message or a call with who it is with, when, the words around the match and the id that opens it; a message says its wire, who wrote it (customer, receptionist or you, as action thread says it, or call note for a call's note in its thread) and its status as action thread says it, and a message of the receptionist's or the team's whose status is queued (held, or not sent yet), canceled (before sending) or failed never reached the customer: say so, never that they were told it; a call says who placed it (called_by). A person's notes are not searched: people with action get reads them. Call action list to find threads by their state, and for what the page on screen does not hold; call action thread when the whole conversation is needed, since a row carries only the last three messages and the page on screen may hold only the thread's row. list returns at most 20 threads, with total_matching counted before the cap, so a count is the total and never the rows shown. thread returns the newest 30 messages, or 80 with more true; a conversation the workspace does not hold is an error, said in words.

partner.name: leads
partner.description: The lead finder and the leads it found, as the Leads page reads it, by action: the searches, the leads in a view, one lead and the people it names, one search, ideas for a new search, and Back today. Action searches takes nothing more and reads the workspace's lead searches, newest first, as the Leads page lists them: what was asked in the owner's words and when, its state or ending in words, how many qualified, need review and were counted, and, for a search that stopped to ask, its question; beside them, the rail's six counts of leads. Read it before proposing a search, so a plan is not repeated, and to answer about a search the person names. A search with a question is waiting for the owner's answer: words that answer it are propose_lead_search with action find and amends set to that search's id, the same plan with the answer applied; to carry on unchanged or stop it, the owner presses Yes, keep going or Stop here on Leads. Action leads reads the businesses the searches found, as a view of the Leads page lists them: list is all (the default), ready, nurture (contacted), converted (talking), said_no or not_a_fit; search_id keeps one search's leads; class is qualified (the default: the counted ones), review (needs review) or excluded (left out), so a lead in review or left out is read only with its class; sort is fit (the default: strongest first), found (newest first), distance (nearest first), business (A to Z), rating (lowest first) or stage (ready first), and dir desc reverses it, so the best rated come first with sort rating and dir desc; words keeps the ones whose name, kind or area has them, as the page's box does. Each lead says its kind, area, class, fit or why it was left out, stage, email, rating, when it was found and its search; with the view's first page come the rail's six counts and, for an owner or a partner, this month's leads used and left. Call it for who the leads are or to find one in a class, and action lead for one lead's details. It returns at most 25 leads, matching counting the view's first five hundred of that class (words match within those) before the cap, and next_page, passed back as after, for the next five hundred. Action lead takes lead_id, the id action leads returned, and an optional search_id to read it as that search found it, and reads one lead as its peek on Leads shows it: its row, what its listing says about it, where it is and whether it is open today, its rating, why it fits, the checks made, where it was found, its phone, email and website. Call it when one lead's details are needed; a lead the workspace does not hold is an error, said in words. Action ideas reads the ideas for a new search Leads keeps for this business: what each finds and where, why this one, and the same search as you would be asked for it. Call it when they ask what to look for, before planning a search. Action back reads Back today: the leads who asked to hear from the business on a day that has come, each with its lead_id, the business, the day and its person where it has one. Nothing writes to them by itself. Action search takes search_id, the id action searches returned, and reads one search as Leads shows it at that search: its row as action searches says it, what the owner asked in their words and what the plan leaves out, how many emails were checked and how many leads have a phone, the qualified by fit (strong, look, long), and where to look next when it ran dry. Call it when one search is named or is the one on screen; a search the workspace does not hold, or one removed from Leads, is an error, said in words. Nothing here starts or changes because it was read, and every string is cut short.

partner.name: people
partner.description: People, the customers and callers, as the People page, a person's page and the Pipeline read them: find people by name or by conditions, a profile, the lists, who wins for this business, and the deals. Action search takes query and an optional list and finds people by name, WhatsApp name, address or three or more digits of a phone number, as the People page searches them; each row says their state in the pages' words, their last contact and last message, their conversation id, channels, consent, receptionist mode, how many calls, their next and last appointment when the calendar is connected, and their next step when they have one. No query lists the most recent people; all finds who conditions hold today, in the lists' vocabulary (who said yes, when they last booked, how they came, a channel, a deal's stage, and the rest propose_list names), counted over everyone; list narrows to one list, given as the token sequences with action lists gives (seg:<id> for People's lists, list:<id> for the workspace's own) or as a People list's bare id: needs_you (Needs you), waiting_on_you (You have it), steps_due (Steps due), new_week (New this week), booked_week (Booked this week), booked (Booked), asked_never_booked (Asked, never booked), lapsed (Lapsed), consultation_booked (Consultations), proposal_out (Proposal out), clients (Clients), deal_passed (Passed), deal_ended (Ended), quiet (Quiet 30+ days), phoned_only (Phoned only), opted_in (Said yes to messages), offers_ok (Can receive offers), opted_out (Opted out). Call it to find someone, or to see who is on a list; it returns at most 12 people, with matches counted before the cap, and a list that cannot be counted here says why. A condition over more than N days holds only for someone with that date on record (never heard from is not quiet): not_on_record counts who meets the rest with no such date, by its chip, and is said apart, never as nobody or as not in People. Action get takes contact_id, the id a row here, inbox with action thread, calls with action get or calendar with action week returned, and reads one person's profile as their page reads it: right now, the facts on file, what is known about them, their receptionist mode, their last exchange, their open conversation, their conversations and calls with ids, their next and last appointments' ids, their timeline, and the team's notes (a note the receptionist suggested is marked so, and is not the team's). Call it when the profile, the timeline or the notes are needed and the page on screen holds only their row; it returns their five newest conversations and calls, twenty timeline entries and twenty notes, and a person the workspace does not hold is an error, said in words. Action lists takes nothing more and reads every list People's rail shows: People's own lists this workspace can count, each with its token (the list action search takes), what it holds and how many are on it; the ones it cannot count here, with why; and the workspace's own lists, kept by hand or by a rule, each with its rule in the page's words and its count or why it cannot be counted, and the archived ones by name. Call it to say which lists there are and how many are on each, and action search with a list's token for who is on it. It counts over everyone in People, as a send counts them. Action winners takes nothing more and reads who wins for this business: how many paid (a deal won), booked (a booking on record) and said yes to offers, then what the winners share against everyone (how they first came, their channels) and, for those a lead search found, what kind of business they were, where, and how they rate. Call it before planning a search for more customers like the best ones, or a list of people like them. Action pipeline takes nothing more and reads the Pipeline as its page builds it: the line over the table (the proposals out, the ones waiting longer than usual, the lapsed, the clients), the workspace's pace, and each group (consultations, proposals out, clients, passed or ended) with its count, what it comes to (the proposals out's and the clients' whole sums, which the page does not show: quote them, never add values up) and its people, each with the deal's id, service and value, how long it has stood there, the page's chip and their next step. Call it for where deals stand, and action get for one person's deal in full. It returns at most 30 people across the groups, the groups' counts whole; a workspace that never recorded a deal has every group empty.

query.description: A name, a WhatsApp name, an address or three or more digits of a number.

list.description: One list: its token (seg:<id>, list:<id>) or a People list's bare id.

all.description: Conditions in the lists' vocabulary, as propose_list takes them: who they hold today.

partner.name: propose_call
partner.description: Propose an act on a phone call in progress, as a card the person approves: a whisper to the phone receptionist, or the call handed to the business's own line. Action whisper takes call_id and text: a sentence only the phone receptionist hears, worked into its next answer to the caller. It shapes what the receptionist says next and never reaches the caller as written. Action hand_over takes call_id and passes the call to the business's own phone: the receptionist tells the caller someone is picking up and transfers them. Call it when they want to take the call themselves. A call that has ended is notLive in words, since there is nobody on the line. Ending a call is the Live page's own button.

call_id.description: A live call's id, from calls with action list and filter live, or the Live page's row.

text.description: The sentence only the receptionist hears, such as: offer Saturday at 10.

partner.name: propose_deal
partner.description: Propose recording a deal on a person: stage proposed (a proposal went out, a new engagement), won (they said yes or paid, now a client), lost (they passed), or ended (the engagement ended). Optional: service, amount_cents with per (once, month or year: a proposal's value, or a client's agreed amount), a note, the proposal's web address (proposal_url), the last day it stands (valid_until, YYYY-MM-DD), with lost only why they passed (lost_reason: price, timing, elsewhere, no_reply, not_a_fit or other), and the next step on it, next_step (what, for the team) with next_step_due (YYYY-MM-DD, today or later), a note with a day the team sees on the deal. Call it when they say a proposal went out, someone became a client, passed or ended; a next step rides on that stage change, never alone, and a move names the open deal's service when there are two. It records what a person told you and never decides money; a move with no open deal to move is refused in words.

input_examples.next_step: Call to walk through the quote

partner.name: propose_follow_up
partner.description: Propose a follow-up of your own, as a card the person approves: a note to come back when something happens (a lead search finishing or stopping to ask, replies on a sequence or a cold email, or a day), or clearing one you came back to. They hold at most 3; signals says a due one first. Action keep keeps a follow-up: said, prompt, wake, and its subject (an id or a plan step's token) or its day. Action clear takes away follow-ups you came back to, by their ids. Offer one after a card whose result comes later (a lead search, a sequence or a cold email started), in the same plan. When a due one is read, do what its prompt says, and clear it beside the cards you make.

said.description: The line they read, at most 100 characters: what you will come back to.

prompt.description: What you will ask yourself when it is due, at most 200 characters.

subject.description: The search's, sequence's or cold email's id, or a plan step's token.

input_examples.said: When the plumbers search finishes, I'll pick the best and draft the emails
input_examples.prompt: The plumbers search finished: pick the best leads and propose a cold email sequence to them.
input_examples.subject: @step:1

partner.name: propose_lead_search
partner.description: Propose finding leads, as a plan card the owner or a partner approves; nothing is searched or spent before that: a new search for businesses or for named people at companies in the US, the owner's answer to a search that stopped to ask, or more for a search that ended. Action find proposes a search for businesses in the US the owner could reach, as a plan card they approve; nothing is searched or spent before that. For named people at companies (marketing managers at agencies), looking_for is people_at_companies: terms their titles (one to five), region their US states or US, who a name for it, count how many companies, and when said seniority (owner, founder, c_suite, partner, vp, head, director, manager, senior, entry), industries (the directory's own names, as Marketing & Advertising, Accounting, Construction, Real Estate; a name it lacks comes back with the nearest) and company_sizes (1 - 10, 11 - 50, 51 - 200, 201 - 500, 501 - 1000, 1001 - 5000, 5001 - 10000, 10001+); nothing else is read. The plan: what kind (who, plural, and who_one, one of them, with category_key as one lowercase word), how many (count: 50, 100, 200 or 500 unless they said a number), where (city with its two-letter region, a zip, or a region alone), the contact standard (contact: phone, or email checked), up to three terms (widest first), the criteria each with whether it is seen or likely and whether it is required, who to leave_out (chains, other kinds; short chips in plain words), looking_for (local_businesses, or people, online_sellers or other when that is what was asked: those are answered in words, not searched), and asked, the owner's words. seen is only for what a listing shows (a rating or review count, a website, an email, a phone that matches the site, open or closed) and is judged from those facts alone; what a business is or does (its kind, who owns it, what it serves or sells, who it treats) is likely, never seen, because a listing's name and category do not count as seeing it, and the kind of business itself is checked on every search without being written as a criterion. Read leads with action searches first, so a plan is not repeated: one plan, never a search. amends is the id of a search that stopped to ask (leads with action searches shows its question) when the plan is that search with the owner's answer applied and everything else kept as it was; the card then answers that search instead of starting a new one. Say the plan in one sentence; never promise how many will be found, and never say a search has started until the card is approved. Only an owner or a partner can approve it: for anyone else, say so and that one of them can ask. Action more finds more for a search that ended (a top-up), or the same search again (renew), on the plan it was made with. Only an owner or a partner can approve it: for anyone else, say so and that one of them can ask.

count.description: How many more to find: 50, 100, 200 or 500 unless they said a number.

search_id.description: The search, from leads with action searches.

renew.description: true to find the same search again from the start, not more of it.

partner.name: propose_leads
partner.description: Propose work on leads, as a card the person approves, by action: a lead's stage or a call's outcome, keep or set aside a search's leads, Later, many leads at once, the address checked again, who a company's email goes to, leads kept as a list to write to, or what a business wrote back. Action stage moves one lead: to ready, nurture or converted (a customer, which makes a person in People), out as not_a_fit (with why) or said_no, emailed (they wrote by hand), or a call's outcome (move call, with outcome, a note and who it reached). Action mark keeps, sets aside or puts back leads of one search (its Needs review pile's acts). Only an owner or a partner can approve it: for anyone else, say so and that one of them can ask. Action later puts one lead under Later, to come back to. Action bulk marks many leads at once: by lead_ids (at most 500), or every lead a view of Leads matches (contacted or not_a_fit), which the door counts itself. Only an owner or a partner can approve it: for anyone else, say so and that one of them can ask. Action addressee chooses who a company's email goes to: one of the people its source named; their address is checked first. Only an owner or a partner can approve it: for anyone else, say so and that one of them can ask. Action list keeps chosen leads (at most 500) as a list of their own, a search a cold email sequence writes to; it spends nothing. In a plan, a cold email step names it by its token. Action said records what a business wrote back to an email sent by hand from the business's own inbox: interested makes it Talking (then propose a deal and a time), a no is never written to again, not_now comes back on its day. Read leads first for the ids. Nothing here writes to a lead: a cold email sequence over a search or a list is propose_sequence with action cold_email, and finding leads propose_lead_search.

partner.name: propose_list
partner.description:
Propose a list on People, as a card the person asking approves, by action: a new list, one that keeps itself current by its rule or one kept by hand with the people they name, one of the workspace's own renamed or its rule changed, or one taken down. Nothing is made until they approve. A list is an audience a sequence or a send can go to, and a line on People's rail; who is on it is counted over everyone in People, as a send counts it, and the card says how many are on it today. A rule is written in the list vocabulary:
Every condition in all must hold for a person to be on the list. A condition is one fact, or { any: [facts] } when one of two to six facts is enough ("on WhatsApp or text"). Use only these fields:
- last_visit: days since their last appointment on the calendar. op more_than or within with days; never or ever without.
- next_visit: days until their next appointment; op this_week is Monday to Sunday of this week. op more_than or within with days; never or ever without.
- missed_visit: days since an appointment they did not come to, as a member marked it missed on the calendar. op more_than or within with days; never or ever without.
- booked: an appointment booked ahead. op is; yes true or false.
- asked_not_booked: wrote or called in the last 30 days and nothing on the calendar answers it. op is; yes true or false.
- last_heard: days since THEY last wrote or called. op more_than or within with days; never or ever without.
- first_contact: days since they first got in touch. op more_than or within with days; never or ever without.
- channel: a way they reach the business: whatsapp, sms, voice (phone calls) or email. op is or is_not; channel.
- came_from: how they first came: whatsapp, sms, email, call, calendar, manual, import or lead. op is or is_not; from.
- calls: how many calls. op at_least or at_most; n.
- conversations: how many conversations. op at_least or at_most; n.
- has_chat: a written conversation either way (no means they have only phoned). op is; yes true or false.
- said_yes: said yes to offers, or to messages (to: offers or messages). op is; to; yes.
- can_receive: can be sent offers or messages: the yes and a number to send to (to: offers or messages). op is; to; yes.
- stopped: asked to stop, or on do-not-contact. op is; yes true or false.
- standing: value needs_you (waiting for a person) or waiting_on_you (a thread you have: you took it over, or your reply paused the receptionist). op is or is_not; value.
- assigned: who has their thread: value me, teammate or nobody. op is or is_not; value.
- deal_stage: where they are on the way to a deal: value consultation, proposed, won, lost (passed) or ended. op is or is_not; value.
- consultation: their next or last appointment is a consultation. op is; yes true or false.
- step_due: a next step whose day has come. op is; yes true or false.
more_than N is more than N days ago (or away); within N is in the last (or next) N days; never is no such moment at all, ever is any.
A month is 30 days, a week 7. 'Regulars' or 'loyal' have no field: say so in cannot rather than invent one.
 Action make takes name and either all (its rule) and cannot, for a new list that keeps itself current, or ids, for a new list kept by hand that starts with the people a read returned ([] for an empty one they fill on People), as People's New list makes one. Call it when they want a group of people kept together, to look at or to send to later: by a rule where what they describe is one, by hand where they name the people. Action change renames one of the workspace's own lists, changes a smart list's rule (all), or both; the card says who it holds after, and its undo puts back what it was. Action delete takes down one of the workspace's own lists; the people stay, and one a campaign runs on, or one other lists are built from, is archived instead, which its receipt says. Read people with action lists first, since a list by that name, or one that says it already, may exist. A rule the vocabulary cannot read is refused in words; what the fields cannot say goes in cannot, never in a fact. People on or off a list kept by hand: propose_people with action list.

Name who by exactly one of all (conditions in the lists' vocabulary, as propose_list takes them), list (a list's token) or ids; the card counts them first, at most 2000, and it goes in parts of fifty. Action answer records the same answer for everyone in a selection, as a class signing up at the desk: only what they said. A yes to offers has to be in writing (form); never record a yes they did not give. Action note adds one line under every selected person's notes, never replacing what is there. partner.name: propose_person
partner.description: Propose an act on one person in People, by action: how the receptionist treats them, a note, a next step with its day, their name or email, their answer to messages or offers, a new person, two records merged, or a first message. A card the person asking approves; nothing changes until they do. Action note takes contact_id, the id a read returned, body, the note in the words to keep (at most 600 characters), and for, who reads it: receptionist, for what should shape how the receptionist answers them (it reads the note before every answer to them), or team, for the team's own reminders and judgments (the receptionist never reads it). Always give for, from their words: it has no default, and the card says it back. Call it for something about one person worth keeping on their page, such as a preference or what to remember next time; a fact about the business itself, such as parking or a policy, is a settings change and not a note, and a next step with a day is not a note: it is action step. Action step sets one person's next step on its own: what to do (at most 600 characters) and the day it is due, today or later, for anyone on the team or for the member asking. It is the team's, shown on their row, the Pipeline and their page and read back by you; the receptionist never reads it. It stands on their open deal (the one whose service is named where they have two), else it is about them. Call it for a reminder or a follow-up with a day ("call Ethan back Friday"); a step that comes with a deal's move rides on propose_deal instead. Action details takes contact_id, the id a read returned, and name, email or both: the name the business calls them by and the address they can be written to, the two fields of their profile. Call it when a customer gave their name or an email address in a message and their profile lacks it or says otherwise; read them first (people with action get), since an address a customer writes back when the receptionist asks for one is kept already, and never propose what the profile holds. It never touches their notes, and the card shows each field as it was and as it becomes. Action answer records what one person said to one of the two questions: messages (about their own bookings) or offers (offers and news): yes, no, or not_asked again, with how they told you. Only what they said: never record a yes they did not give. A yes to offers has to be in writing (form, or customer_message naming the message), and a spoken yes covers messages alone; a no is honoured however it came. Action add puts someone in People by hand: a phone, an email or both, and a name. Nobody is messaged by adding them and their answers start as not asked; a number or address already in People opens that person instead. Action message writes first to someone in People: a new conversation on a channel their answers allow now, in the member's words or, where only a message WhatsApp approved can go, that message by name. Use propose_reply for a thread that waits on an answer. The card says the channel and who has the thread after; it leaves 15 seconds after it is approved and can be cancelled within them.

partner.name: propose_plan
partner.description: Propose a plan of several cards from one call, approved as one: an offer or a whole setup of the customer journey, made from the workspace itself; or any steps across pages you name, each a card of an act tool, building on one another. Action offer makes every card an offer or a whole setup takes, from one call: intent offer, with offer (words, the offer in their words, its days named as a customer reads them on its first day: “all November”, never “next month”; from and until, its first and last day, YYYY-MM-DD by the business's calendar; service, who as a list token, and channels, each optional) and say, their own phrasing of the offer where they gave one, its days named as words names them, never the ask (“I want to offer”); or intent cover_journey, with optional stages, for a campaign on each moment of the journey not covered yet, and what they told you of their business: books, what their customers book in their own words (“discovery call”), and proposals true where they said some customers get a proposal before they buy. The plan says what must be connected or turned on first for the moments it cannot start yet, and leads the answer with it. Name what they asked for and the days they gave, never an id or a time to send: the plan reads the Library, the lists, the campaigns, the notes, the calendar's room and the channels itself, and reuses a message that fits or writes one in language (en or es, as the rule for a message's language says; left out, the business's). It comes back as the plan's words and its steps, each its own card in order: those that send nothing (a message, a note for the receptionist, a pause) are approved together, and each send on its own after them; answer from the plan's words once they come back, and never say any of it is done. Action steps makes a plan across pages from the steps you name: each a card of any act tool, by its tool, action and its own input, a later step naming what an earlier one makes by its token (@step:n: a list, a list of leads, a message, a sequence, a search). The steps that change only what the workspace keeps are approved together; each that sends, spends or posts is its own press after them. Call it when one ask takes several cards that build on each other (organize people into lists, a cold email to a list of leads with a follow-up, a sequence and its first steps); for an offer or a whole setup of the journey, action offer. Call it alone, with no answer beside it: its result comes back with the plan's words, and you write the answer from them. Never say any of it is done.

partner.name: propose_reply
partner.description: Propose a reply to a customer, as a card the person approves before anything is sent. Action draft takes conversation_id, the id a read returned, text, the reply itself, and voice, you for the person's own words or receptionist for the receptionist's voice, and proposes a new reply on a thread, on the wire the thread runs on. Action steer takes message_id, the held draft's id from inbox (with action list or thread), never a conversation id, and instruction, a rewrite in words ('shorter', 'mention Saturday is full', 'in Spanish') of a reply the receptionist is holding; the rewrite waits its turn like the first draft. Action booking answers a booking the receptionist asked for in a thread (a hold that says Asked for a time): booked true books it and drafts the reply they send, booked false lets the time go and leaves the thread waiting on their reply. It takes the thread's conversation_id; one with no request waiting is refused in words. Call action draft when they ask to reply, answer or write to someone, and action steer when they want a held draft changed. draft refuses a person who opted out and marks a closed reply window on the card; never quote or confirm a price in the text. steer refuses in words a reply that is no longer waiting, so read the thread first when in doubt.

partner.description: Propose a reply to a Google review, as a card the person approves; it is posted publicly under the review once approved. Action reply takes review_id and comment and proposes the business's public reply under that review. Read the review first (report with lens reviews). Thank them by what they said, answer a complaint plainly and offer to make it right by phone or message; never argue, never name a customer's private details, never offer money or a discount.
