owner.name: propose_sequence
owner.description: Propose what sends on its own, as a card the person approves (every such thing is a sequence): a message sent once, a sequence at a moment of the customer journey or on a list, a whole new sequence with its steps, a step added, changed, taken away or given new words, a draft started or let go, people taken out, a batch waiting for an OK approved or skipped, a sequence paused, resumed, renamed or retimed, its channels, a new saved message, and cold email to leads. Action once takes template_id, one message (the id of any of its versions, as sequences with action lists lists it), and proposes sending it to an audience, everyone whose yes covers it (a reminder or a confirmation the yes to messages, an offer or news the yes to offers) or any list sequences with action lists names (audience_kind everyone; list for a People list, with its id as audience_id; saved for one of the workspace's own, with its audience_id), with params as the message's values in order (typed text, or @first_name, @business_name, @booking_link or @review_link, the link its Google listing keeps for a review, to fill per person), an optional scheduled_for as an ISO time with its offset (2026-09-20T15:00:00-04:00, never a bare date), an optional name, and optional channels (whatsapp, sms, email; whatsapp when none is named, so for a message that holds email or text name the channels its `channels` in sequences with action lists say it holds): each person is reached once, on the first it can, and a channel the workspace cannot send on, or the message has no version for, is refused. Action moment takes trigger and proposes a standing rule that sends one message to newly eligible people who said yes: trigger is quiet_30 (win-back by silence, nothing heard in 30 days, where no calendar is connected), lapsed (win-back by appointments, none in 45 days, where a calendar is connected), visit_tomorrow (a reminder the day before an appointment) or visited (a check the day after one), both only where a calendar is connected and each sent whatever else the person hears from you within a week of it, everyone_monthly (the month's offer), saved_list (on any list: its token from sequences with action lists in list, one of People's or one of the workspace's own, with policy_class campaign for an offer or reengage for a win-back), or proposal_waiting (the proposal follow-up: one nudge per proposal waiting past the workspace's pace, one such playbook per workspace, its message carrying the proposal's link as @proposal_link), a moment this workspace is not offered being refused in words to say; template_id is a message from sequences with action lists (the id of any of its versions), or omitted for the trigger's starter, which the card adds at its Approve where the workspace does not hold it yet (its WhatsApp version then goes to WhatsApp for review where none is on file, which the card says), but for a starter that takes words of its own such as the month's offer; starter, in place of template_id, is the moment's starter to file at Approve where the workspace does not hold it yet, by its key: on visited, after_visit_review is the thank-you with a review ask, only where the Google listing keeps a review link, and after_visit_check, the thank-you that asks how it went, is the one taken when none is named; params are the message's values in order (typed text, or @first_name, @business_name, @booking_link, @review_link, the link its Google listing keeps for a review, @visit_when and @visit_service on an appointment's moment, or @proposal_link), filled in for a starter except a typed one such as the month's offer; run_hour is 9 to 20 by the business's clock (default 10), cap_per_run defaults to 25, and channels (whatsapp, sms, email; when none is named it goes by every one the workspace can send on now that the message holds, as a new playbook opens in Campaigns, and the card says which, so name them only to go by fewer, or by one that is not ready yet) are the ones it may go by, each person once on the first it can: a channel its purpose never carries is refused, and one the workspace cannot send on yet is kept, its runs holding those people until it can; until is its last day, YYYY-MM-DD by the business's clock, today or later, after which it runs nothing. A new one starts with the mode its class's Autonomy row says (decision 0064), and its first batch waits for an OK whatever that is, which the card says. Action make proposes a whole new sequence to customers: first, its first step exactly as action moment takes it (a moment or a list, its message by template_id, its clock and channels), then up to 3 steps after it (each a wait, what must still hold, its message), and start (true starts it once approved, false keeps it as a draft). Write each message first with action message where the Library has none, in a plan. Action step adds a step after the last (after_days and template_id), or changes one after the first by step_id: its wait, what must still hold, its channels, name or values. A step's message is changed with action words. Action step_remove takes away a step after the first, with the steps after it. Action words gives a step a different message from now (write it first with action message); where WhatsApp has to approve it, the step keeps sending its own until then. Action start turns a draft on: its first step runs from its next run. A paused one is resumed with action change. Action run_now runs a sequence's first step now, as its hourly run would: it waits for an OK where its class asks. Action change takes playbook_id, a playbook that exists, as sequences with action moments gives it (or the page's rows), and only what they asked to change: state (paused stops its next runs; running starts them again under its own mode), name (at most 80 characters), run_hour (9 to 20 by the business's clock), cap_per_run (1 to 500 people a run), gap_days (7 to 365 days before a person is reached again), cadence_days (1 to 90, the month's offer alone), params (its message's values in order, as action moment takes them: new text in the same message, never a new message), until (its last day, YYYY-MM-DD by the business's clock, today or later; it runs nothing after) or mode (how its batches are decided, its "Before each batch": ask, each waits for an OK; veto, each waits 30 minutes for a Stop, then goes; auto, each goes on its own, never for a sequence to leads; a batch of new words waits for an OK whatever it says). Nothing else about it moves: its moment, message and list are its drawer's, and its channels are action channels'. A run already waiting for approval stays waiting after a pause, and the card says so: propose action batch with verb skip beside it when they want that run gone. A sequence to leads (cold email) takes state and mode alone here, its emails and steps being its page's; anything else asked of one, a value outside its bounds and a playbook that already reads so are refused in words; a part of the change it already holds (a pause of one paused) is left off the card, which says so, and the answer says it too. Action channels takes playbook_id, a playbook that exists, as sequences with action moments gives it, and channels (whatsapp, sms, email), every channel it should go by from now on, not only the ones to add (that read gives the channels it goes by now): each person is reached once, on the first of them that can reach them, so one more channel widens who it reaches and never sends a person two messages. Nothing else about the playbook changes. A channel its purpose never carries is refused; one it cannot go by yet (no line, no version of its message there, offers by email not open) is kept, and the card says it waits and that its runs hold those people until it can; a run of it already waiting for approval keeps the channels it was made with, and the card says so; and a playbook that already goes by exactly those channels is refused in words. Action batch takes broadcast_id, a playbook's run that waits for a person, as sequences with action moments (a playbook's waiting) or action sent (waiting_on_you) gives it, and verb: approve, which sends it now (asked outside the hours a message may go out in, between 9:00 and 20:59 by the business's clock, it goes at 9:00), or skip, which ends this run unsent and leaves the playbook running. Always give verb, from their words: it has no default, and the card says it back. A run made for a day that has passed can only be skipped, and a batch to leads (cold email) is approved or skipped the same way, its card saying what the check held. Action leave takes people or leads out of a sequence; a send of theirs not yet gone is skipped with them. Action decide answers an email the check held: include lets it go as it is, rewrite writes its opening again, skip leaves it out of this batch, not_a_fit sets its business aside. Nothing undoes it. Action sent_by_hand records what became of an email handed over to send by hand from the business's own inbox: sent, or not_sent. Ask them; never say one went that they did not say. Action discard takes away a draft that never sent; one that has been on is paused instead. Action message writes a new message for the Library and proposes it as a card: name (snake_case), language (en or es, as the rule for a message's language says; another language is another card under the same name, called together), category marketing (an offer or the business's news) or utility (about their own appointment or proposal, which needs a whatsapp version), versions, each optional and at least one (whatsapp {body}, email {subject, body}, sms {body}, never sms for marketing), and slots naming the values {{1}}, {{2}} in order (position, label, kind: text, first_name, business_name, booking_link or review_link). Read sequences with action messages first: a name the Library holds in that language is refused. A whatsapp version needs a connected number and goes to WhatsApp's review; email needs email set up. Your versions are a first draft that the message writer rewrites before the card is shown: put the facts in them (the offer in their words and figures, its days), never a price they did not give. The card quotes every version; Approve files it, and nothing is sent. Action cold_email proposes a cold email sequence to the businesses of a search or a list of chosen leads (propose_leads with action list makes one): its emails, their waits and its pace, from the workspace's own mailboxes (or handed over to send by hand). Its first run is planned once approved and waits for their say before an email goes. Write like a person to one business; never claim a relationship that does not exist. Action leads adds leads to a reach-out fed by a list (one made from leads chosen or imported, not a search's own): root_id is the reach-out's id (reach_out on leads with action lead, or the reach-out the page has open), lead_ids the leads' ids from leads. The card says first what the add would do -- how many would join and why each other would not (already written to, a customer, no checked address, with another reach-out) -- by the add's own rule, and is refused in words when none would. It sends nothing and approves no run: the reach-out's next run plans the first email and waits for their say. A reach-out a search keeps current is refused: its search's new leads join it by themselves. For an offer, a promotion or a whole setup, call propose_plan with action offer instead. Read sequences first: action list and action sequence for what exists and its ids, action lists for who can be sent and the messages a send may use, action moments for the moments offered. When nobody can be sent a message, say why: nobody said yes (point to their profiles) or the ones who did have no number to send to, or no channel that can carry it now (the lists read says which); never propose a send to nobody. A starter the workspace does not hold yet is added at the card's Approve, a typed value left blank is refused in words, and a second running sequence on the same moment, list and message is refused unless they name it apart. A person reads campaign or sequence, never playbook or broadcast; the fields keep those names.

owner.name: propose_settings
owner.description: Propose a settings change as a card the person approves, by action: what the receptionist knows (closed days, hours, a note, a service), how it answers (its voice, languages, what callers hear and who they reach, your own words, the messages when it can't answer, photos), what it may do alone for a class of message (autonomy), or the business's goal for you. Action change takes one change object: add_closure (date, an optional until for a range, and an optional note), set_hours (one weekday's day with open and close, or both empty for closed), add_note (a title, the text the receptionist reads, and an optional until, its last day), or add_service (name, and an optional duration_min in minutes). Dates are YYYY-MM-DD, days mon..sun, times HH:MM. Call it when they say they are closed, their hours change, the receptionist should know something, or they offer a new service. Only an owner or a partner can approve it: for anyone else, say so and that one of them can ask. Action answers takes one row object, a row of How it answers and what it becomes: set_tone (tone, how it sounds in a line; empty takes it away), set_languages (languages, the whole list it speaks, which replaces the one it has; empty for none), set_phone_greeting (greeting, the line callers hear first, {business} for the name; empty for the standard one; a line that never says it is automated has the product's clause added when spoken), set_phone_voice (voice, one of Tamsin (Woman · American), Grace (Woman · American), Nia (Woman · American, younger), Willa (Woman · British), Claudia (Woman · Mexican), Nico (Man · American), Jack (Man · American), Alejandro (Man · Mexican, younger)), set_transfer_number (number, with its country code like +1 212 555 0143, a line a person answers; empty and it takes a message instead), add_own_words (text, added after the owner's own words, which it reads on every reply), set_message (which, one of error (it couldn't write a reply), non_text (it got something it can't read), greeting (the ai is down), and text, with {business}, {booking link} and {phone} filled as it goes out; empty for the product's wording), set_photos (on, whether it looks at the photos customers send on WhatsApp). Read workspace.settings first for what each row holds now: a list replaces, so keep the languages they did not ask to drop. Call it when they want it to sound, speak, greet, put callers through or answer differently. Only an owner or a partner can approve it: for anyone else, say so and that one of them can ask. Action autonomy changes what the receptionist may do alone for a whole class of message: class with mode, or the reply confidence dial (min_confidence) alone. Call it when they want the receptionist to act on its own, wait for them, or hold its replies for a look; propose_person with action mode is for one person. Each class takes the modes its row on the Autonomy page offers (veto holds a reply, or the reply to a review, so a person can stop it), and a mode a class does not take is refused in that page's words. For reengage, campaign and follow_up the row is what a NEW sequence starts as (decision 0064): each existing sequence keeps its own mode, changed by propose_sequence's change with its mode; a sequence that should not send is paused, so those rows take no never. Never for money: that class is locked by charter, so a request to change it is answered in words, not proposed. The modes as they stand are in this prompt above, so no read is needed first. Action goal keeps the owner's goal in one line (at most 200 characters), which you read on every question and weigh every suggestion and plan against; empty clears it. Call it when they say what they want the business to reach, or ask you to aim for something. The receptionist never reads it. Only an owner or a partner can approve it: for anyone else, say so and that one of them can ask. Action answer_style keeps how this person likes your answers (length, format, language) as their own note, which comes with each of their questions from then on; empty clears it, and it replaces the one they keep. Call it when they want answers a way beyond this conversation ("always bullets", "every time in Spanish", "next time, shorter"); a shape asked for within one conversation is kept there without it. Theirs alone, never a teammate's, and they see and change it in Settings › Profile.

owner.description: Propose an Inbox action on a thread: take_over (a person answers from here), hand_back (the receptionist resumes), snooze (until an ISO time with its offset, or by default tomorrow at 10:00 by the business's clock), wake, archive, or resolve (close the open escalation; the thread stays). conversation_id is the id a read returned. Call it when they ask to take, hand back, snooze, wake, archive or resolve a thread; a reply is propose_reply with action draft, and how the receptionist treats one person is an owner's to set (propose_person with action mode). It refuses in words when the action does not fit the thread's state: nothing to resolve, not snoozed, or nobody to hand back from.

owner.name: report
owner.description: The Reports page for any window its period control picks -- a period (7d, 30d, 90d or month: month is the days since the 1st), days picked (from and to, YYYY-MM-DD, at most ninety, ending today at the latest), or a shortcut (yesterday, last_week, last_month), 30d where none is named -- and only the lenses asked for (lenses: overview, campaigns, reviews, cold_email, receptionist, people; every one where none is named). The overview: messages answered by the receptionist, by a person and left unanswered, the median and p90 reply time (both include the hold the owner set before a reply goes out; reply_time.hold splits the replies against it: with no hold, as the hold ended, or later, and the most any took past it), calls and their minutes, new people, the escalation reasons, the change against the period before, a by-day series, the booking line (asked, then booked) where the calendar is read, the Deals section where a deal was ever recorded, and the Campaigns lens, as the page says it: head is its sentence; figures are the people sent to, the share of the messages delivered, the share of those people who wrote back, and the yeses and stops after a campaign, each against the period before; funnel is what was sent, delivered, read (WhatsApp's alone) and answered, counted in messages (a person sent three is three messages here and one in figures); by_channel is the same by channel where more than one sent (read is a share of what went by WhatsApp alone: a text or an email keeps no read receipt); sources are the five that sent the most; window is the period's, from the database's ledger: held (who was held back, and why), runs_stopped (the runs that failed or were canceled), failed_sends (why sends failed after they left), by_message (who wrote back to each message), send_to_first_reply (how soon the first reply came) and wait_for_your_ok (how long approvals waited); stuck is what is stuck now, whatever period is picked: the runs waiting for your OK, the failed runs, the replies waiting on you, the messages Meta stopped and your WhatsApp number; a share is said only of five or more and a count under that, and a mix with nothing to draw says the page's words in empty; window is null where the database does not keep the ledger yet and stuck where it does not keep what is stuck, each with an error beside it where its read failed, and a part of window the database did not count is null too; campaigns says error where its numbers could not be read. The Reviews lens is in reviews: the sentence at its head and its figures as the page says them (the rating, the count, the reviews written against the period before) and, where the owner's Business Profile is connected, how many were answered and how fast, the mix of stars, and how many wait for a reply (held is how many of the oldest waiting hold a reply the receptionist wrote and did not post), the oldest five waiting in rows and the newest five in latest, each with its id; reviews says linked false where no Google listing is linked, and error where its numbers could not be read. The Reach-outs section is in reach_outs, as the page says it: strip is the emails the reach-outs wrote, the share that landed and the number that bounced, each against the period before; emails is what was written, delivered and bounced, counted in emails; businesses is the businesses written to and how many wrote back, were interested, booked or said no, counted in businesses as they stand now (each counts once, at the last email that wrote to it, and an outcome is set against nothing before); angles is who wrote back, as they stand now, by the opening of the last email; handed is the line on the businesses handed to the owner, null where none were, and empty says nothing was written; reach_outs is null where the workspace has no reach-out, and error where its numbers could not be read. The Receptionist lens is in receptionist, as the page says it: what became of the replies held before they went out (hold), what customers asked about (topics), the languages the receptionist wrote in where it wrote in more than one, how the calls someone spoke on ended, the booking link and how many of the people it went to have booked since (link), your first reply after a handover and the time to settle one (handover), the missed calls answered within an hour (missed), what came while the business was closed and how many of those the receptionist answered (closed), and what is stuck now (stuck: who waits on you, call-backs, the replies held back), with held_back giving the reasons the send door refused a reply; receptionist says available false where the database does not keep these numbers yet, and error where they could not be read. The People lens is in people, as the page says it: head is its sentence; window is the period, counted in people (one who wrote ten times is one): reached (who reached you, how many were new, the yeses won and the stops, each against the period before), channels (how they reached you), first_came (how the new ones first came), yeses and stops (who gave them), steps_done (the steps finished and how many on their day) and email_stopped (the addresses that stopped working); book is everyone as they stand now, whatever period is picked: wires (the ways they reach you), fresh (how long since they last wrote or called, with quiet saying how many have been quiet over 30 days), stuck (the steps overdue and due today, and the email that stopped working) and stand (how many said yes to messages, can receive offers, opted out or are quiet); a mix with nothing to draw says the page's words in empty; people says window null where the database does not keep the period's numbers yet, book null where the people could not be counted, available false where neither could be read, and error where they could not be read. Call it for how a period went or for a trend, naming only the lenses the question needs; the today tool has the day itself and its counts, and the Reports page on screen already holds this. An empty period says so in empty; a window the report cannot answer is an error, said in the page's words.

owner.name: sequences
owner.description: Everything that sends on its own, as Campaigns reads it (every such thing is a sequence), by action: the sequences, one sequence's steps and people, the moments of the customer journey a sequence can start at, who a send can go to and the messages it may use, the Library, what went out and how it did, the journey, and cold email to leads. Action list reads every sequence as the Sequences page lists them: each with its sequence_id, name, group, what starts it, state, line, steps and who is in it, and what waits on the owner (needs_you); needs_you on top is the page's count. Action sequence reads one as its record shows it: when it starts and stops, the mode its batches go under (and batches_did: what its batches did over the last 90 days, how many went after an OK or on their own, stopped or skipped unanswered: the evidence a mode is set on), its one notice, its steps with their ids (wait, message, channels, last 30 days), who is in it by where they stand (in_it: the first 25, each with its contact_id or lead_id), what waits on the owner (waiting_on_you: each held or handed-over email by its send_id, for propose_sequence with action decide or sent_by_hand), and its last five batches. Action moments reads the sequences that start at a moment as the page shows them, standing rules that each send one message to newly eligible people who said yes: each with its playbook_id, what starts it, its message (template), its channels, its clock and next run (next_run, null where it runs nothing: runs_nothing says why, and ended the day one ended), its last day ahead (ends), its state in the page's words, its own mode (mode: how its batches are decided, mode_words says each, and next_batch_asks_first where its next batch waits for an OK because its words are new), its list when it runs on one, what it sent and how many replied over the last 30 days (null where that could not be read), and a batch waiting for a person; then every moment this workspace can use, with who it names now: said_yes_now (who said the yes its message needs, a number or not) and can_be_sent_now (who of them a run reaches), and each one's starter message. Action lists, read before any send, lists who a send may go to: everyone who said yes, every People list this workspace can count, and every list of the workspace's own, each with its kind and audience_id (what propose_sequence with action once takes), its list token (what people with action search takes), and four counts, because there are two consents and a yes needs a number to send to and a channel to carry it: can_be_sent_offers and can_be_sent_messages (who a promotional, or a utility or authentication, message reaches on WhatsApp) and said_yes_to_offers and said_yes_to_messages (everyone who gave that yes, as People counts it, whether or not a number or a channel can carry it now), with why_none_offers or why_none_messages where some said yes and WhatsApp reaches none of them, saying what they lack in People's words. It says which channels carry offers now (offers_go_by), and also lists, under templates, the messages a send may use, each with its template_id (any of its versions' ids names the message), category, channels (true for each of whatsapp, email and sms it can be sent on now; a message that holds email or sms is proposed with channels naming them, and its card then counts the people those channels reach, so a 0 in the four counts above does not mean nobody can be reached), values and body, why a WhatsApp version this product cannot send whole is left out (cannot_send), and whether the number may send and its daily limit, since a send reaches only a recorded yes with a number to send to. Action messages reads the Library whole: every message, a name in a language, with its category, each version on its channel with its state (approved, pending while WhatsApp reviews it, rejected, paused or disabled), the values it fills and the sequences that send it (used_by). Call it before a new message is written, so the Library never holds a twin; to pick a message a send can use now and say who it reaches, call action lists instead. Action sent reads what went out as the page lists it, the recent fifty, with older saying whether there are more: each batch with its name, whether a campaign or a person sent it, who it went to and its message, its state in the page's words (one waiting for a person to approve it has waiting_on_you; one whose day has passed is too_late_to_approve), when, how many it was for, how many were sent (sent_by_channel, where it went by more than one), the share of those delivered, the share of those sent by WhatsApp that were read (a text or an email keeps no read receipt), and how many replied, were held back and failed, with why one failed. Action batch reads one batch as its opened run shows it: its row, the five figures (sent, delivered, replied, said yes, asked to stop), the people it touched in the page's words, and what came back, quoted. It returns at most 20 people and 10 replies, the figures counting everyone. Action journey reads the customer journey: how many of its moments are covered (covered, of), then each stage in the order a customer passes it (first contact, the day before and the day after an appointment, which need a calendar, a proposal waiting where a deal was ever recorded or a sequence stands on it, quiet or lapsed) with whether it is covered, its state, the moment a sequence on it starts from and the sequences that stand on it; and guide, what each touch point sends and when. An offer or a whole setup is one call of propose_plan with action offer, which reads the journey itself and makes the steps, never a sequence proposed stage by stage from this read. Action cold_emails reads the cold email sequences to leads: each with its root_id, name, the search or list of leads it writes to, whether it runs, its emails, its pace, whether the owner sends each from their own inbox, and who is in it (waiting, writing, done). Read action lists before a send, and to say who a message would reach; action moments to say what is running, and before a new sequence at a moment. Pick the message first, then quote its can_be_sent count as who it reaches, never a larger one, for a message that goes by WhatsApp; for a message whose channels hold email or sms, propose it with channels naming them and quote the card's count, since the can_be_sent counts are by WhatsApp alone and a 0 there does not mean nobody can be reached; when a WhatsApp message's count is 0 and its said_yes is not, and its channels hold no other, the ones who said yes cannot be sent it: say how many said yes and what they lack, as the audience's why_none words say it (a number to send to, or a channel that can carry it, which offers_go_by names), and never send the owner to get a yes they already have. When a moment's can_be_sent_now is 0 and said_yes_now is not, the ones who said yes have no number to send to, no channel that can carry it now (action lists' offers_go_by names which), or hear from you within a week of today: say so the same way. A list that cannot be counted here carries cannot_count and no counts; a null count means the page could not count it just now, and nothing has run because it was read. A person reads campaign or sequence, never playbook or broadcast; the fields keep those names.

sequence_id.description: A sequence's id, from action list.

broadcast_id.description: A batch's id, from action sent or a moment's waiting batch.

owner.name: signals
owner.description: What stands out across the workspace now, computed from its pages, each with its numbers and the cards that fit it: a follow-up of yours that is due, people with nothing sending on its own, lists that feed nothing, leads nobody writes to, a search that asks a question, replies and batches waiting, people never asked for the yes to offers, deals with no next step; and the owner's goal. Read it at the start of a conversation, when they ask what to do next or how to get more customers, and before proposing a plan of your own. It takes nothing and changes nothing.

owner.name: today
owner.description: The Today page as it stands: who needs a person right now, the WhatsApp threads whose free-reply window is closing while the customer waits, today's calls, the standing of the receptionist, a recap and the day's counts. Start here for 'how are we doing', 'what needs me' or 'brief me', and read it for what Today holds when the person is on another page. needs_you counts the holds and the replies counting down to send in your name (replies_on_their_way, which it does not list: inbox with action list has them); campaign_runs_waiting are the runs waiting for your say: those an approval can still send, and going reach-out runs whose check holds emails for you (sequences with action sent lists them); going_today is what goes on its own later today unless it is stopped (a batch held for a stop, a message sent once and set for later, a reach-out's run), each with when it goes, as Today's Going today draws it; searches_waiting stopped to ask you. It holds no drafts: inbox with action list and filter held has them, and inbox with action thread has a whole conversation. Nor the bell's notifications, what was sent to this person: workspace with action notifications reads them. needs_you and calls are capped, the counts are not; nothing changes because it was read.

owner.name: workspace
owner.description: The workspace, by action. Action settings takes nothing more and reads the settings as the receptionist runs on them: the business and its time zone, hours, closures, services, languages, guardrails, notes, booking rules, when it escalates, whether the calendar and vision are on, the notifications (where alerts are emailed), the autonomy rows with their modes and limits (the reply policy's dials among them), and which channels are connected with their numbers. Call it for the reply policy's dials, the channels and the notifications; the hours, closures, services, notes, guardrails, booking notes and the autonomy modes are already in this prompt, so answer those from here without a read. A channels read that failed is said in could_not_read, never as no channels; propose_settings is what changes a setting. Action connections takes nothing more and reads what the workspace is connected to, in the Setup page's words: whether the receptionist answers and on which numbers; its phone line and whether the number its customers know is forwarded to it, WhatsApp, the email mailbox, the calendar and Google, each with its state and what the page says of it; and each mailbox it writes its reach-outs from, with its state, its day, its ramp and what to do next. Call it for whether something is connected, or why not; action settings has the receptionist's own rules. Billing and the plan's price are not here: money stays out of Ask. Action notifications takes nothing more and reads this person's own notifications as the bell keeps them on the server: the last thirty days, sixty at most, newest first, each with its title, its first line, how long ago, whether it is unread for them and where it opens, and how many are unread; one they dismissed is gone. Call it for what the bell has told them. The bell also shows what the page works out in the tab (threads waiting on a person, missed calls, invitations), which this cannot read, so say the bell may hold more; billing's notices stay out of Ask. Action activity takes an optional person (a contact_id a read returned), kind (a verb or an event kind, exactly as the log spells it), day (YYYY-MM-DD, by the business's clock) and cursor (the next_cursor an earlier read returned), and reads who did what, as Settings › Activity lists it: both ledgers, newest first, each with when, who and what in the page's words, and where it opens; the usage, webhook and ingest records only when their kind is asked for. Call it for what a member or the receptionist did, and when. It returns the newest 30, with next_cursor for the ones after them while there are more; anything about money (billing, a partner's share) stays out of Ask. Nothing changes because it was read.
